questions.stem: Which of the following statements accurately describes a difference between the Cyber Kill Chain and Mandiant's Attack Life Cycle?

options.text: Attack Life Cycle treats attacks as "one and done"; Cyber Kill Chain does not
Cyber Kill Chain treats attacks as "one and done"; Attack Life Cycle does not
Cyber Kill Chain focuses on reconnaissance; Attack Life Cycle does not
Attack Life Cycle focuses on reconnaissance; Cyber Kill Chain does not

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Cyber Kill Chain treats attacks as "one and done"; Attack Life Cycle does not

The Cyber Kill Chain is a popular information security framework developed by Lockheed Martin. The framework is based on the different steps an attacker takes to select, infiltrate, and take actions against a target. 

The Cyber Kill Chain consists of 7 phases. The 7 phases in order from first to last are:

Reconnaissance: The attacker researches, identifies, and selects a target(s)
Weaponization: The attacker prepares malicious software and/or payloads
Delivery: The attacker transmits the weaponized software to the target(s)
Exploitation: The weaponized software's code is triggered to perform exploits on the target(s)
Installation: The weaponized software installs backdoors and/or enables persistent access to the target(s)
Command & Control: An outside system communicates with the compromised target system(s) to provide the attacker with control inside of the target network(s)
Actions on Objective: The attacker performs actions to achieve their primary objective (e.g., data destruction, data exfiltration, additional intrusions, etc.) 

The Attack Life Cycle was created by cybersecurity firm Mandiant. It includes the following stages:

Initial reconnaissance 
Initial compromise
Establish foothold
Escalate privileges
Complete mission 

Importantly, the fourth phase includes a cycle of performing reconnaissance, moving laterally (east-west) within a network, maintaining presence, and further escalating. This cyclic step differs meaningfully from the Cyber Kill Chain which takes a more "one and done" view of attacks.

Correct answer: Bluesnarfing

Bluesnarfing is an attack where the attacker gains unauthorized access to a device to steal information such as contact lists, calendars, emails, and text messages. 

Bluejacking only involves sending unsolicited messages. Bluebugging allows an attacker to take full control of a device. Bluesmack is a denial-of-service attack.

questions.stem: Which evasion technique involves altering the case of SQL keywords to evade case-sensitive security filters?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Case Variation

Case Variation (also called Case Mutation) is an evasion technique where attackers alter the case of SQL keywords to bypass security filters that are case sensitive. By changing the typical uppercase presentation of SQL keywords to mixed or lower case, the attacker can evade filters that are not configured to recognize keywords in variant cases. 

Dynamic Querying, Command Delinking, and Operator Camouflaging do not specifically refer to the alteration of keyword cases as a method of evasion.

The threat actor is working to exploit what principle of influence made popular by Robert Cialdini?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Authority

Robert Cialdini famously proposed six principles related to influence, which can help CEH candidates better understand social engineering. They are:

Reciprocity - People have a tendency to repay favors or kind acts
Commitment - Once someone commits to something, they are more likely to do it
Social proof - If others are doing something, people find it more acceptable to do the same
Authority - People generally follow instructions from, or are highly influenced by, others in a perceived position of authority 
Liking - People have a higher probability of doing something if they like the person delivering the message
Scarcity - A limited supply or availability of something makes it more desirable

questions.stem: What is one way to quickly determine that systems on a target network are alive?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Perform a ping sweep

Performing a ping sweep is one way to quickly determine which systems are alive on a target network. A ping sweep is when you send ping messages to every system on the network. Tools such as fping and MegaPing can be used to perform ping sweeps. 

Many vulnerability scanners can tell you if a system is alive or not as well, but it will not be as quick as running a ping sweep. A packet crafting tool, such as hping, can be used to craft packets in a specific way that may be used to evade firewalls or other detection methods. Fragmenting packets will not assist in quickly determining which systems are alive.

A high FRR does not imply a high rate of allowing unauthorized access.

questions.stem:
During an authorized network assessment, a tester uses the graphical version of packETH. The tester needs to load several different packets from packet capture files and transmit them as part of one traffic sequence.

Which packETH window should the tester use?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Gen-s

The Gen-s window in packETH is used to send different types of packets. The tester can select packets previously created in the Builder or imported from packet capture files and configure how the packet streams are transmitted. This makes Gen-s the appropriate choice for generating a sequence composed of different packets.

Builder is used to create or modify an individual packet and send that packet once. It does not provide the multi-packet sequence function described.

Gen-b sends multiple copies of the packet currently defined in Builder. It is appropriate for repeated transmission of one packet rather than a sequence containing different packets.

Pcap loads and displays packets from a packet capture file so that an individual packet can be selected and opened in Builder. It is not the window used to transmit the configured sequence.

questions.stem:
Employees report that a wireless network with the same Service Set IDentifier (SSID) as the organization’s legitimate network has appeared nearby. The unauthorized access point attempts to attract users and capture authentication information before forwarding their traffic.

Which attack is occurring?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Evil twin attack

An evil twin attack uses a rogue access point configured to imitate a legitimate wireless network, including advertising a known Service Set IDentifier (SSID). Users who connect may expose authentication information or send traffic through the attacker-controlled access point.

A deauthentication attack sends forged management frames to disconnect wireless clients and force them to reconnect. It does not by itself create a rogue access point that imitates the legitimate network.

A key reinstallation attack manipulates the wireless handshake to cause reuse of an encryption key. It does not rely on advertising the legitimate network’s SSID through a rogue access point.

Wireless footprinting identifies nearby wireless networks and gathers information such as SSIDs, channels, and signal strength. It is a reconnaissance activity rather than an access-point impersonation attack.

questions.stem: Which attack could occur if a cloud service provider has not properly isolated network traffic between tenants in a multi-tenant environment?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Traffic sniffing

Traffic sniffing can occur if network traffic is not properly isolated in a multi-tenant environment, allowing an attacker to capture network traffic from other tenants. The service provider should ensure that the tenants' networks are properly isolated and secured to prevent this type of attack.

VLAN hopping exploits weaknesses within Virtual Local Area Networks (VLANs). ARP spoofing poisons the ARP cache to reroute local network traffic. Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks overwhelm services with traffic but do not exploit a lack of network isolation.

questions.stem:
A consultant receives administrative credentials for several Windows servers. The consultant needs to identify missing security updates, insecure local configurations, and known software vulnerabilities while gathering detailed remediation information.

Which tool should the consultant use?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Nessus

Nessus is a vulnerability scanner that uses plugins to examine systems for known vulnerabilities, missing updates, and insecure configurations. Credentialed scans allow it to inspect Windows hosts more thoroughly and produce findings that include severity, supporting details, and potential remediation guidance.

Nmap primarily discovers hosts, ports, services, application versions, and operating systems, although its scripting engine can perform some vulnerability checks.

Metasploit is primarily an exploitation framework used to validate and exploit vulnerabilities, although it also includes some auxiliary scanning modules.

smbclient provides command-line access to Server Message Block (SMB) shares and services rather than conducting a comprehensive vulnerability assessment.

After employees leave for the evening, an attacker searches bags awaiting collection outside an office building. The attacker also records the locations of exterior cameras and employee entrances for possible use in a later assessment. The bags contain printed customer records, internal directories, and notes with account information.

Which social engineering activity is the attacker primarily performing?

options.text: Tailgating to enter a restricted facility
Eavesdropping to obtain information from conversations
Dumpster diving for discarded sensitive documents
Shoulder surfing to observe sensitive information

Correct answer: Dumpster diving for discarded sensitive documents

Dumpster diving involves searching discarded materials for information that an organization failed to destroy securely. Printed records, internal directories, credentials, and account details may support identity theft, impersonation, or later attacks.

Shoulder surfing involves watching a person enter or view sensitive information. The attacker is examining discarded materials rather than observing an employee.

Tailgating involves following an authorized person through a controlled entrance. The attacker is gathering information outside the building rather than attempting to enter it.

questions.stem: You want to see if you are able to get any information about the applications in use on target 192.168.10.111 by having nmap look at the application banner. Which command could you run to achieve this?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: nmap -sV 192.168.10.111

Version scanning, using the -sV parameter in nmap, is one way to gather information about applications. The command nmap -sV 192.168.10.11 would run a version scan on the host 192.168.10.111. When running a version scan, nmap connects to the port and issues the correct protocol commands to get the application banner. The banner may include information such as the software or application name as well as the version. 

The command nmap -sS 192.168.10.111 will perform a SYN scan of the target. The command nmap -sN 192.168.10.111 will perform a NULL scan of the target. The command nmap -sT 192.168.10.111 will perform a full TCP connect scan of the target. Only the version scan will provide information about the applications.

questions.stem: Which social engineering attack involves an attacker pretending to be a legitimate entity to extract sensitive information from a victim?

Tailgating involves an attacker seeking entry into restricted areas by following closely behind a legitimate user. Eavesdropping is the act of secretly listening to conversations, and dumpster diving involves searching through trash to find valuable information.

The -sP flag was a former flag used for the same purpose, but in recent versions of Nmap, it has been replaced by -sn. The -sT flag initiates a TCP connect scan, while -sU initiates a UDP scan.

questions.stem: Which mode of operation in DES can encrypt plaintext to produce completely different ciphertext even when the same plaintext block is encrypted multiple times?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Cipher Block Chaining (CBC) mode

Cipher Block Chaining (CBC) mode uses an Initialization Vector (IV), and each plaintext block is XORed with the previous ciphertext block before being encrypted, ensuring that the same plaintext will produce a different ciphertext with each encryption. 

Electronic CodeBook (ECB) mode does not have this property, as it encrypts identical plaintext blocks into identical ciphertext blocks. Cipher FeedBack (CFB) mode and Output FeedBack (OFB) mode also use feedback mechanisms, but CBC is the most recognized for this particular feature.

questions.stem:
A video circulating on social media appears to show a public official announcing an unexpected policy change. The image and speech appear realistic, but the post does not identify the original recording, and no official channel has published the announcement.

Which action would provide the strongest basis for determining whether the video is authentic?

options.text: Inspect several frames for compression artifacts or inconsistent image quality
Confirm whether established accounts have reposted the same video
Assess facial motion and lip synchronization for signs of manipulation
Trace the original source, and verify the claim through official records

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Trace the original source, and verify the claim through official records

Tracing the source chain and corroborating the claim through independent records evaluates both the origin of the media and the surrounding context. Synthetic media may appear convincing, so authenticity should not depend on one visual characteristic or the number of reposts.

Natural facial movement does not establish authenticity because modern deepfakes can reproduce realistic expressions and synchronization.

A compression artifact may result from ordinary encoding or repeated uploads and does not independently prove manipulation.

Reposting by established accounts may amplify the content without confirming that those accounts verified its origin.

questions.stem:
While reviewing server logs, a network engineer notices a drastic spike in DHCPDISCOVER requests using broadcast address 255.255.255.255. 

These logs are a strong indicator of what potential attack?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: DHCP starvation 

DHCP starvation attacks work by an attacker making many DHCPDISCOVER requests to a legitimate IPv4 DHCP server by using the broadcast address 255.255.255.255 and not responding to the DHCP offers. Eventually, the legitimate server runs out of available IPv4 addresses. 

This attack is a type of denial-of-service attack. It can be used in conjunction with a rouge attacker-controlled DHCP server that can then provide bogus DHCP responses to legitimate clients on the network. This allows the attacker to define network settings for clients and supports various session hijacking attacks. 

Directory (or path) traversal is an attack where an attacker attempts to access files and directories outside of a web server's jailed root directory. 

DHCP spoofing is a generic term that implies an attacker is spoofing the address or domain of a DHCP server.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a capability of sslstrip?

Legacy encryption like SSL v3 or TLS 1.0 typically can be decrypted by sslstrip. 

These decryption capabilities allow it to downgrade HTTPS connections to HTTP.

sslstrip is not intended to reverse hashing functions like SHA1.

questions.stem:
A network-based vulnerability scan identifies exposed services on a Linux server but provides little information about missing local patches, insecure file permissions, or vulnerable installed packages. The analyst configures the next scan with valid Secure Shell credentials.

What additional capability do the credentials provide?

options.text: They allow the scanner to install missing security patches
They allow the scanner to check for local vulnerabilities
They guarantee that every reported finding is exploitable
They allow the scanner to bypass network firewalls

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: They allow the scanner to check for local vulnerabilities

Valid Secure Shell credentials allow a vulnerability scanner to authenticate to the Linux server and inspect information that is not normally visible through remote network probing. This can include installed software, missing patches, local configurations, file permissions, and other host-level weaknesses. OpenVAS is one example of a scanner that can use supplied credentials to perform these authenticated local checks.

Credentials do not allow the scanner to bypass network firewalls. The scanner must still be able to reach the target through permitted network paths and services.

Authentication does not guarantee that every reported finding is exploitable. Scanner results still require analysis and, when appropriate, manual validation.

A vulnerability scanner identifies and reports potential weaknesses. Providing credentials does not automatically authorize or cause the scanner to install patches.

questions.stem:
A cryptanalyst examines a long message encrypted with a simple substitution cipher. One ciphertext character appears much more frequently than the others. The cryptanalyst compares the character distribution with the normal frequency of letters in English to identify likely substitutions.

Which technique is being used?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Frequency analysis

Frequency analysis compares how often characters appear in ciphertext with the known statistical distribution of letters in a language. In a simple substitution cipher, frequently occurring ciphertext characters may correspond to common letters such as e, helping the cryptanalyst infer the substitutions.

Brute-force analysis attempts every possible key or transformation until meaningful plaintext is produced. It does not primarily rely on comparing character-frequency patterns.

Differential cryptanalysis studies how differences in selected inputs affect differences in the resulting ciphertext. It is not the statistical letter-distribution method described in the scenario.

Pattern-distribution analysis is not a recognized cryptanalytic technique.

questions.stem: What defensive measure can help mitigate the risks associated with DNS poisoning attacks?

options.text: Limiting the number of hops in a traceroute
Applying MAC filtering on network devices
Using DNSSEC to validate DNS responses
Using VPNs exclusively for all online activities

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Using DNSSEC to validate DNS responses

DNS Security Extensions (DNSSEC) adds an additional layer of security by providing cryptographic signatures for DNS data, ensuring the authenticity and integrity of the DNS response, which in turn can help mitigate the risks associated with DNS poisoning attacks. 

MAC filtering, VPN usage, and limiting traceroute hops do not directly defend against DNS poisoning.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of DNSSEC in relation to DNS responses?

options.text: To enable password protection for DNS responses
To enhance the speed of DNS responses
To provide cryptographic signatures for verifying the authenticity of DNS responses

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: To provide cryptographic signatures for verifying the authenticity of DNS responses

Domain Name System Security Extensions ( DNSSEC) provides cryptographic signatures that are used to verify the authenticity of DNS responses. It is designed to protect against DNS spoofing and cache poisoning attacks. Attackers can enumerate DNSSEC using nmap.

DNSSEC does not enhance the speed of responses, enable password protection, or encrypt the responses.

questions.stem:
A suspicious executable has no reliable antivirus signature. During analysis, it launches an unusual child process, creates a new file in a temporary directory, and opens an outbound connection to an unfamiliar host.

Which conclusion is best supported by these findings?

options.text: The unusual child process provides enough evidence to identify the malware family
The outbound connection provides enough evidence to confirm malicious activity
The combined behaviors provide stronger evidence of malicious activity than any single indicator
The temporary file provides enough evidence to confirm ransomware activity

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: The combined behaviors provide stronger evidence of malicious activity than any single indicator

Correlating multiple behavior types provides stronger evidence than relying on a single event that may also occur during legitimate software activity. Process actions, file changes, and network connections together can reveal a malicious execution pattern even when a reliable signature is unavailable.

An outbound connection can occur in legitimate applications and does not by itself prove malicious behavior.

Creating a temporary file does not establish that the program is ransomware.

An unusual child process may be suspicious, but it does not by itself identify a specific malware family.

questions.stem: How do MDM solutions typically enforce encryption on mobile devices?

By using third-party messaging apps for communication

questions.stem: Attackers who use a large number of tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) to gain access to an environment and remain within that environment for as long as they can are known as which of the following?

Hacktivists are attackers who attack with a political cause in mind. An insider threat, also known as a malicious insider, is an employee of an organization who knowingly or unknowingly puts the company's security at risk. Script kiddie is a term often used to describe an inexperienced hacker who uses tools created by others to hack into systems.

questions.stem:
An organization wants to encrypt and digitally sign email using a vendor-neutral specification that can be supported by multiple compatible products rather than relying on one implementation.

Which characteristic of OpenPGP meets this requirement?

options.text: It provides digital signatures without supporting message encryption
It defines an open standard for interoperable encryption and digital signatures
It relies exclusively on symmetric keys shared between correspondents
It requires X.509 certificates issued by a centralized certificate authority

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: It defines an open standard for interoperable encryption and digital signatures

OpenPGP defines a publicly available standard for encrypting and digitally signing messages and files. Multiple products can implement the standard, allowing users of compatible software to exchange protected information without depending on a single implementation.

Requiring X.509 certificates from a centralized certificate authority describes a certificate-based trust model such as the one commonly used with S/MIME, whereas PGP-based systems traditionally use a web of trust.

OpenPGP supports both digital signatures and encryption, so its capabilities are not limited to verifying message authenticity and integrity.

OpenPGP uses a combination of asymmetric and symmetric cryptography rather than relying exclusively on preshared symmetric keys.

questions.stem: In the web application vulnerability stack, what does the term " XSS" stand for?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Cross-site scripting

In the web application vulnerability stack, XSS stands for Cross-Site Scripting. It is a security vulnerability that allows attackers to inject malicious scripts into content from trusted websites, which is then executed in the victim's browser. XSS attacks can lead to user session hijacking, website defacement, or phishing expeditions. 

XSS is not related to server styling, server security settings, or XML syntax.

questions.stem:
Alex, a systems engineer at Acme Inc., is trying to determine why an Apache web server went offline and stopped serving requests to users. 

Alex debugs the system and learns that a system was sending incomplete HTTP headers that caused Apache to leave connections open. As a result, the server used all available TCP connections and stopped answering requests from legitimate clients. 

What type of DoS attack was performed on the system? Choose the most specific answer.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Slowloris 

Common denial-of-service (DoS) attacks CEH candidates should be familiar with include: 

Bandwidth: A category of attacks that attempt to exhaust bandwidth to cause service to drop or degrade. Bandwidth attacks are typically symmetric in the amount of resources required from the attacker vs. the target.
Amplification: A category of attacks that are asymmetric in the amount of resources required from the attacker (low) vs. consumed on the target (high)
Smurf: A type of amplification attack that uses ICMP (e.g., ping requests)
Distributed: DoS attacks with multiple systems participating in the attack 
Slow: A category of attacks that typically take some time to deny service and typically require a relatively limited amount of resources
Slowloris: A specific type of slow attack that sends incomplete HTTP headers to webservers

The question correctly describes the manner in which slowloris attacks use incomplete HTTP headers to exploit vulnerable servers.

questions.stem:
Malware has been confirmed on one endpoint, and telemetry shows it attempting connections to several additional internal systems. The investigation has not yet determined the full scope of compromise.

Which response should take priority?

options.text: Restore the endpoint from backup before determining whether spread is still occurring
Isolate the infected endpoint from other systems while the investigation continues
Continue collecting evidence while leaving the endpoint fully connected
Wait for the malware family to be identified before restricting connectivity

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Isolate the infected endpoint from other systems while the investigation continues

Host isolation limits the compromised endpoint’s ability to reach additional systems while investigators determine the incident’s scope. This reduces the chance of further propagation without requiring the complete investigation to be finished first.

Leaving the endpoint fully connected preserves the same path the malware is already attempting to use for further spread.

Waiting for exact malware-family identification delays a control that can immediately limit additional compromise.

Restoring the endpoint before controlling active spread can remove local evidence while leaving other potentially affected systems or propagation paths unaddressed.

questions.stem:
During an authorized web application assessment, a penetration tester captures an authenticated user’s session cookie and submits it from another browser. The application grants access to the user’s account without requiring the tester to enter the user’s credentials.

Which attack has the penetration tester demonstrated?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Session hijacking

Session hijacking occurs when an attacker obtains a valid session identifier and uses it to assume control of an authenticated session. As described in the reference, session-identification information stored in cookies may allow access to websites where the victim has privileges. Replaying the captured cookie lets the tester access the user’s session without entering the user’s credentials.

Token manipulation involves altering or forging a token to change how an application interprets it. The tester reuses an existing valid session cookie rather than modifying or creating one.

Session fixation causes a victim to authenticate using a session identifier that the attacker already knows. This scenario instead involves capturing a cookie after the user has authenticated.

Cross-site request forgery causes an authenticated user’s browser to submit an unintended request. It does not involve the attacker replaying the user’s session cookie from another browser.

questions.stem:
A security engineer is hardening a service against attackers who attempt to inject forged packets into established Transmission Control Protocol connections. The defense must make it difficult for an attacker to calculate valid sequence values for a connection they cannot observe.

Which control most directly addresses this risk?

options.text: Assign static source ports to clients

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Generate unpredictable initial sequence numbers

Transmission Control Protocol uses sequence and acknowledgment numbers to track data exchanged during a connection. Generating unpredictable initial sequence numbers makes it difficult for an attacker who cannot observe the traffic to calculate acceptable values and inject forged packets into the session.

Assigning static source ports makes connection details more predictable and does not protect the sequence-number space.

Increasing the maximum session duration keeps connections active longer and may increase the opportunity for an attacker to target them.

Using fixed acknowledgment intervals does not prevent an attacker from estimating valid sequence values. Predictability would weaken rather than strengthen protection against forged-packet injection.

questions.stem: What option can be added to an hping3 command to send packets as quickly as practical without a delay between them and is useful for testing several types of denial-of-service attacks?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: --flood

The --flood option causes hping3 to send packets as quickly as possible without displaying replies. It can be used during authorized testing to generate a high packet rate and evaluate how a target handles denial-of-service conditions.

The -S option sets the SYN flag in TCP packets. It changes the packet type but does not remove the delay between transmitted packets.

The -f option fragments transmitted packets. It does not cause hping3 to send them at the maximum possible rate.

The --tos option sets the IP type-of-service field. It does not control the transmission speed.

An attacker performs one suspicious action every several hours. Each endpoint, identity, DNS, and cloud-security product records activity below its individual alert threshold. The organization’s XDR platform still generates a high-confidence incident.

Why was the evasion unsuccessful?

options.text: XDR treated every new DNS query as confirmed malicious behavior
XDR lowered every individual product threshold until each event generated an alert
XDR blocked all activity that occurred outside normal business hours
XDR correlated the individually weak signals into a meaningful cross-layer sequence

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: XDR correlated the individually weak signals into a meaningful cross-layer sequence

XDR can correlate low-confidence signals across endpoints, identities, networks, and cloud services. Events that appear harmless in isolation may reveal a recognizable attack sequence when their relationships and timing are evaluated together.

Lowering every threshold is not required and could substantially increase false-positive volume.

Activity outside business hours may contribute context, but it is not automatically malicious.

questions.stem:
A technician must establish a long-distance, point-to-point wireless link between two buildings. The antenna must concentrate the signal into a narrow beam, provide high directional gain, and be precisely aimed at the receiving site.

Which antenna is best suited for this deployment?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Parabolic grid antenna

A parabolic grid antenna focuses radio-frequency energy into a narrow, highly directional beam. Its high gain and focused radiation pattern make it well suited for long-distance, point-to-point wireless links in which the transmitting and receiving antennas can be precisely aligned.

A dipole antenna has a comparatively broad radiation pattern and is commonly used for general wireless coverage rather than a narrowly focused long-distance link.

A reflector antenna uses a reflective element to direct or strengthen the signal from another antenna. Although it can increase directionality, it does not identify the specific high-gain parabolic grid design described.

An omnidirectional antenna distributes radio-frequency energy across a broad horizontal area. It supports coverage around the antenna rather than concentrating the signal toward one distant receiver.

questions.stem:
Alfonso is attempting to enter a building that he doesn't have authorized access to be in. The doors to the building use badge readers, but Alfonso doesn't have a badge. Alfonso decides to wait around the entrance for an employee to run their badge and enter so that he can sneak in behind them. 

What is the name of this technique?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Tailgating

Tailgating is a common technique used to gain unauthorized entry to buildings and facilities. Tailgating entails waiting around by commonly used entrances for an employee, or anyone with valid access, to unlock the doors to enter. Once the door has been unlocked and the individual with access enters, the person tailgating sneaks in behind them without asking for permission. 

Piggybacking is similar to tailgating, but in a piggybacking situation, the individual with authorized access consents to allowing the unauthorized individual to "piggyback" off their access. Shoulder surfing is a social engineering technique to obtain information by viewing a screen over an individual's shoulder without them noticing. Dumpster diving is the act of looking for sensitive documents and information that may have been thrown out in the trash by a target.

questions.stem: Which principle of Robert Cialdini's theory of influence theorizes that if someone agrees to do something either verbally or in writing, they are more likely to follow through with it?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Commitment

Robert Cialdini proposed six principles as part of his theory of influence: reciprocity, commitment, social proof, authority, liking, and scarcity. These concepts are useful when conducting social engineering. The principle of commitment is that, if someone commits to something either verbally or in writing, they are more likely to follow through with it.

The principle of social proof outlines that when you see someone doing something, such as using a specific product, you will see that it is acceptable to use that product as well. Reciprocity refers to the idea that people will generally feel obligated or want to respond to an act of kindness or a favor. Scarcity refers to the lack of availability of something making it seem more valuable.

questions.stem: What is the main concern with sensitive data exposure in web applications?

options.text: Faster depletion of server bandwidth due to heavy traffic
Unauthorized disclosure of financial, healthcare, or personal information
The need for more frequent updates to the application's content

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Unauthorized disclosure of financial, healthcare, or personal information

The main concern with sensitive data exposure is the unauthorized disclosure of sensitive information such as financial data, healthcare records, or personal details, which can lead to identity theft, fraud, and other forms of cybercrime. This vulnerability arises from inadequate protection of sensitive data, such as encryption at rest or in transit. 

Sensitive data exposure doesn't typically cause increased traffic, server costs, or the need for content updates.

In Nmap, the -v flag is used to enable verbose mode, the -sU flags are used for UDP scanning, and -sP for performing a ping sweep.

questions.stem:
An attacker steals a valid session token after a user signs in to a sensitive application. The application periodically reevaluates the device, user context, and risk level and requires reauthentication when those conditions change.

How does this control affect the attack?

options.text: It changes the token into an encryption key for the application session
It guarantees that the attacker’s first request with the token will be rejected
It prevents the attacker from copying the token from the user’s browser
It limits how long the stolen token remains sufficient to maintain access

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: It limits how long the stolen token remains sufficient to maintain access

A stolen token may initially represent an authenticated session, but periodic re-evaluation can require fresh proof when risk or context changes. This reduces the period during which possession of the token alone is enough to continue the hijacked session.

Re-evaluation occurs after token theft and does not itself prevent the original token from being copied.

A session token identifies or authorizes a session; contextual verification does not convert it into an encryption key.

A valid stolen token may be accepted initially, so the control does not guarantee rejection of the first malicious request.

A session token identifies or authorizes a session; contextual verification does not convert it into an encryption key.

A valid stolen token may be accepted initially, so the control does not guarantee rejection of the first malicious request.

questions.stem: Which cryptographic principle ensures that an operation cannot be reversed to reveal the original input?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Hashing

Hashing is a cryptographic principle ensuring that an operation cannot be easily reversed to reveal the original input, which makes it a one-way function. Hash functions are designed to take an input (or message) and return a fixed-size string of bytes, typically a digest that is unique to each unique input. 

Key exchange is a method used to securely exchange cryptographic keys between two parties. Non-repudiation is a way to guarantee that someone cannot deny the authenticity of their signature on a document or a message that they send. Symmetric encryption is a type of encryption where the same key is used for both encryption and decryption, which by nature is reversible.

Network sniffing isn't used to encrypt data packets, establish a VPN connection, or audit firewall configurations.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an effective countermeasure against ARP spoofing attacks?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Utilizing static ARP entries

Using static ARP entries means setting a device to only recognize a specific IP-MAC address pairing. This is effective against ARP spoofing attacks because the device will not accept unsolicited ARP responses that try to associate a malicious MAC address with a known IP. 

While MAC address filtering can add a layer of security, it doesn't directly combat ARP spoofing. Limiting bandwidth and reducing DHCP lease times are unrelated to ARP spoofing countermeasures.

Two endpoints are infected by the same malware family. On a finance workstation, the malware prioritizes financial documents for encryption. On a marketing workstation, it generates internal-looking phishing messages based on information available on that host.

Which characteristic best explains the different behavior?

options.text: The malware is adapting its actions to the context of each compromised system
The malware is relying exclusively on commands predetermined before the infections occurred
The malware must contain a different fixed payload for every possible workstation
The malware is changing only its file signature while keeping its actions identical

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: The malware is adapting its actions to the context of each compromised system

Agentic malware can use AI to evaluate its environment and choose actions based on the context it finds. Selecting valuable files on one system while generating locally relevant phishing lures on another demonstrates adaptive decision-making rather than a single predetermined behavior path.

A different fixed payload for every workstation is unnecessary when the malware can determine actions dynamically.

Changing a file signature describes polymorphism but does not explain why the malware performs different tasks on different systems.

Predetermined commands would produce a more fixed workflow and do not account for decisions made from information encountered after compromise.

questions.stem: A cryptanalyst is evaluating why the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) is resistant to linear and differential cryptanalysis. Which AES design characteristic contributes most directly to this resistance?

options.text: Repeated nonlinear substitution and diffusion operations
Use of a fixed 128-bit block size
Generation of paired public and private keys
Support for multiple symmetric key lengths

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Repeated nonlinear substitution and diffusion operations

AES processes data through multiple rounds that combine nonlinear substitution with operations that spread changes throughout the data block. The nonlinear substitutions complicate attempts to model relationships between plaintext, ciphertext, and keys, while diffusion prevents input patterns from remaining localized.

A fixed 128-bit block size defines how much data AES processes at one time but does not by itself provide resistance to linear or differential cryptanalysis.

AES supports 128-, 192-, and 256-bit keys, which affect resistance to exhaustive key searches rather than supplying the cipher’s primary defense against these forms of cryptanalysis.

Public and private key pairs are used in asymmetric cryptography, whereas AES is a symmetric block cipher that uses the same secret key for encryption and decryption.

Which finding most strongly indicates ARP poisoning?

options.text: The gateway IP is being mapped to an unauthorized workstation MAC address

The workstation is resolving several hostnames through the DNS server
The gateway is renewing its address through normal DHCP operation

ARP poisoning inserts a false IP-to-MAC mapping into local ARP caches. Mapping the gateway’s IP address to an employee workstation redirects traffic through that system and enables interception or manipulation.

Domain Name System (DNS) resolution maps names to IP addresses rather than IP addresses to MAC addresses.

A legitimate switch-table update may follow a device movement, but it would not make an unrelated workstation appear as the default gateway in ARP caches.

questions.stem:
An IoT sensor network relies on reports from multiple nodes to select trusted routing paths. Investigators discover that one compromised device is presenting dozens of different node identities, allowing it to influence routing decisions as though it represented many independent devices.

Which attack is occurring?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Sybil attack

A Sybil attack occurs when one malicious device claims multiple false identities within a distributed network. Those identities can give the attacker disproportionate influence over routing, voting, trust calculations, or other decisions that assume each identity represents a separate device.

A sinkhole attack attracts nearby traffic by advertising an especially favorable route, causing other nodes to forward data through the malicious node.

A wormhole attack captures traffic at one network location and tunnels it to another location, creating the appearance of an unusually short routing path.

A hello flood attack transmits powerful discovery or greeting messages that convince distant nodes the attacker is a nearby routing neighbor.

questions.stem: Which of the following options accurately describes the purpose of the host command?

A security analyst is evaluating a symmetric encryption algorithm that was an Advanced Encryption Standard finalist. The algorithm uses a 128-bit block, supports 128-, 192-, and 256-bit keys and operates as a 16-round Feistel network with key-dependent substitution boxes.

Which algorithm is being evaluated?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Twofish

Twofish is a symmetric block cipher that was one of the five Advanced Encryption Standard finalists. It uses a 128-bit block, supports 128-, 192-, and 256-bit keys and operates as a 16-round Feistel network with key-dependent substitution boxes.

Serpent was also an Advanced Encryption Standard finalist, but it uses a 32-round substitution-permutation network rather than the 16-round Feistel structure described.

Rijndael was selected as the Advanced Encryption Standard. It uses a substitution-permutation structure with 10, 12, or 14 rounds depending on the key size rather than a 16-round Feistel network.

Blowfish is a 16-round Feistel cipher designed by Bruce Schneier, making it a plausible alternative. However, it uses a 64-bit block rather than the 128-bit block described.

During an authorized assessment, a tester submits a database query through a vulnerable web application. The application displays no query results or database errors, but the database server sends a Domain Name System (DNS) request to a tester-controlled domain containing encoded query data.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Out-of-band SQL injection

Out-of-band SQL injection retrieves data through a communication channel different from the one used to deliver the malicious query. In this scenario, the payload is submitted through the web application, but the database returns information through a Domain Name System request to a tester-controlled server.

Error-based SQL injection extracts information from database error messages returned through the application. The scenario states that the application displays no database errors.

Boolean-based blind SQL injection infers information by observing changes in the application’s response to true-or-false conditions. It does not rely on a separate network channel to return data.

Time-based blind SQL injection infers information by causing conditional delays and measuring the application’s response time. The scenario instead describes data leaving through a DNS request.

questions.stem: Why are kernel-level rootkits particularly concerning for system administrators?

options.text: They operate at a low level, making detection and removal extremely challenging
They require physical access to the machine
They always corrupt the hard drive

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: They operate at a low level, making detection and removal extremely challenging

Kernel-level rootkits embed themselves in the operating system's kernel, which is the core of the OS, allowing them to operate at a very low level. Due to their deep integration with the system, they can effectively hide their presence and manipulate system operations, making them extremely challenging to detect and remove. 

The statement that they only target outdated software is inaccurate, as rootkits can target both outdated and current software, depending on their design. While some forms of attacks might require physical access, kernel-level rootkits can be installed remotely. Rootkits' primary purpose is stealth and persistence; they do not always corrupt the hard drive, as doing so would draw attention to their presence.

A web application uses values from a contact form to construct and send an email. A tester inserts a carriage return and line feed into the sender field, followed by an additional Bcc field. The resulting message is delivered to recipients who were not specified by the application.

Which attack does this demonstrate?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Email header injection

Email header injection occurs when a web application incorporates unvalidated input into an email message. By inserting carriage return and line feed characters followed by another SMTP header, an attacker may add recipients or otherwise alter the message generated by the application.

OS command injection causes an application to pass attacker-controlled operating-system commands to a command interpreter. It does not manipulate the headers of an email message.

A buffer overflow occurs when a program writes more data to a memory buffer than it can hold. The scenario involves altering message structure through unvalidated input rather than exceeding a memory boundary.

SQL injection places database commands or query fragments into application input to manipulate a backend query. It does not append SMTP fields to an email generated by the application.

questions.stem: What is the name given to the type of malware that is used to install other malware types, such as backdoors, botnet clients, and key loggers, to a system?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Dropper

A dropper is a malware type that is used to deliver or install other types of malware on a target system. Some malware types that a dropper might install include backdoor software, botnet clients, and keyloggers. The purpose of using a dropper rather than directly installing the malware is that a dropper may be able to avoid detection better than the other malware types. 

Worms, viruses, and ransomware are other types of malware, but they are not used to install other types of malware on a system in the way that a dropper does.

questions.stem: In the context of web server security, what is the purpose of implementing a WAF?

options.text: To filter and monitor HTTP traffic between a web application and the internet
To verify user identity through CAPTCHA challenges
To encrypt data between the client and server
To detect and remove malware from the server

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: To filter and monitor HTTP traffic between a web application and the internet

A Web Application Firewall ( WAF) is designed to filter and monitor HTTP traffic between a web application and the internet, protecting the web server from various attacks such as SQL injection, Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), and others by blocking malicious traffic. 

Encryption of data is handled by protocols like SSL/TLS, CAPTCHAs are for distinguishing between humans and bots, and antivirus software is used to detect and remove malware.

Which AI application vulnerability best explains the finding?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Sensitive information disclosure

Sensitive information disclosure occurs when an AI application exposes confidential, personal, proprietary, or otherwise protected information through its responses. The evidence here is unauthorized disclosure of another employee's data rather than control of the model itself.

Model theft involves unauthorized extraction or copying of the model rather than disclosure of protected information contained in a response.

Insecure plugin design concerns weaknesses in connected tools or interfaces, such as inadequate authorization or unsafe parameter handling.

Excessive agency involves granting an AI system too much authority to perform actions rather than exposing protected data in generated content.

questions.stem:
A vulnerability scan identifies that an internet-facing web server is running a software version the vendor no longer supports. The vendor will not release additional security patches for that version.

Which action should the administrator take?

options.text: Apply the last available security patch to the current version
Enable automatic updates for the current version
Upgrade the software to a currently supported version
Remove unused modules from the current installation

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Upgrade the software to a currently supported version

Unsupported software no longer receives newly developed security fixes from its vendor. Upgrading to a supported version restores access to ongoing patches and addresses the underlying software-lifecycle risk.

Applying the last available security patch may correct vulnerabilities discovered before support has ended. It does not protect the server from vulnerabilities discovered after the vendor stopped releasing updates.

Automatic updates cannot deliver new vendor patches for a version that is no longer supported.

Removing unused modules reduces the server’s attack surface. Vulnerabilities can still remain in the unsupported software components that continue to run.

questions.stem:
Two testers use the same AI assistant against comparable environments. Each receives a different sequence of suggested tests, and neither records the prompts, assumptions, nor validation steps used.

Which change would most improve the reliability of future assessments?

options.text: Accept the different sequences as evidence that the assistant is adapting correctly
Place the AI-assisted steps inside a documented, repeatable testing methodology
Use the assistant only after exploitation has already been completed manually
Allow each tester to select whichever generated steps appear most efficient

questions.explanation:

A documented methodology makes testing consistent, repeatable, and verifiable even when an AI assistant generates variable recommendations. Recording prompts, assumptions, and validation steps also allows another tester to reproduce and evaluate the process.

Different output sequences may reflect adaptation, but without documentation and validation, they cannot be reliably compared or reproduced.

Individual judgment remains useful, but an undocumented selection process does not create consistent assessment coverage.

Restricting AI use to a later phase does not solve the underlying lack of repeatability.

questions.stem:
An organization’s wireless IoT sensors suddenly lose connectivity whenever an unauthorized device begins transmitting continuous high-power signals across the sensors’ operating frequency. The sensors remain powered, and the tester observes no forged management frames or rogue access points.

Which attack is disrupting the sensors?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Radio-frequency jamming attack

A radio-frequency jamming attack disrupts wireless communications by transmitting interference on or near the frequencies used by legitimate devices. The continuous high-power signal prevents the IoT sensors from reliably transmitting or receiving data, creating a wireless denial-of-service condition.

A deauthentication attack uses forged wireless management frames to disconnect clients from an access point. The scenario states that no forged management frames are present.

A replay attack captures legitimate wireless transmissions and sends them again later. It may cause unauthorized actions or authentication problems, but it does not normally disrupt communications by continuously saturating the radio frequency.

An evil twin attack uses a rogue access point that impersonates a legitimate wireless network to attract users or devices. The scenario contains no rogue access point.

questions.stem: Why is UDP scanning generally slower and less reliable than TCP scanning?

options.text: Because UDP scanning uses ICMP echo requests
Because UDP always requires a three-way handshake
Because UDP scans rely on the RST flag
Because UDP is connectionless and doesn't provide acknowledgments

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Because UDP is connectionless and doesn't provide acknowledgments

UDP is a connectionless protocol and does not offer the same acknowledgments as TCP, making scanning less reliable, as there's no guarantee of receiving a response. As a result, the scan will also take longer than a TCP scan.

UDP does not require a three-way handshake and does not rely on the RST flag (these are both associated with TCP). ICMP echo requests are related to ping operations, not specific to UDP scanning.

questions.stem: What is the primary distinction between a virus and a worm in the context of cybersecurity?

options.text: A virus is always harmful, while a worm is always benign
Viruses and worms are synonymous terms in cybersecurity
A virus requires user intervention to propagate, while a worm can replicate itself automatically
A worm requires user intervention to propagate, while a virus can replicate itself automatically

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A virus requires user intervention to propagate, while a worm can replicate itself automatically

The primary distinction between viruses and worms is their propagation mechanism. A virus typically requires user intervention, like running an infected file, to propagate, while a worm can self-replicate and spread without user action. 

It's inaccurate to categorize viruses as always harmful and worms as always benign; both can have detrimental effects. Worms and viruses are not synonymous terms in cybersecurity; they have distinct characteristics.

A zero-day vulnerability is a flaw that is unknown to those responsible for patching or fixing the flaw and not about configurations. A design flaw pertains to a deeper, intrinsic issue in the way a system or application was designed. A third-party risk arises due to dependencies on external software or entities, not due to configuration settings.

questions.stem:
During an authorized cloud security assessment, a tester exploits a flaw in the virtualization layer and executes code outside a guest virtual machine, gaining access to the underlying host.

Which type of vulnerability enabled this virtual machine escape?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Hypervisor vulnerabilities

A hypervisor manages virtual machines and enforces separation between guest systems and the underlying host. A vulnerability in this virtualization layer may allow code executing inside a guest virtual machine to cross that isolation boundary and affect the host or other virtual machines. This type of compromise is known as a virtual machine escape.

Unpatched guest Operating System (OS) vulnerabilities may allow an attacker to compromise the virtual machine itself, but they do not inherently provide access outside the guest environment.

Insecure cloud Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) may expose cloud resources or administrative functions, but the scenario specifically describes escaping through the virtualization layer.

Misconfigured network access controls may permit unauthorized communication with cloud resources, but they do not directly allow code inside a guest virtual machine to cross into the host.

questions.stem: What is a recommended security practice when configuring Wi-Fi on mobile devices?

options.text: Use VPNs when connecting to public Wi-Fi networks
Connect to open Wi-Fi networks to avoid overuse of cellular data
Frequently change Wi-Fi networks to prevent tracking
Disable SSID broadcasting to make the device invisible

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Use VPNs when connecting to public Wi-Fi networks

Using a Virtual Private Network (VPN) when connecting to public Wi-Fi networks is a recommended security practice, as it encrypts traffic and protects against eavesdropping. This is essential because public Wi-Fi networks are often a target for network sniffing.

Open Wi-Fi networks should be used cautiously, disabling SSID broadcasting is not applicable to client devices, and frequently changing Wi-Fi networks does not inherently improve security.

questions.stem:
A cloud-hosted prediction service accepts input through an authenticated API and returns both a classification and a confidence score. The assessment team suspects that a customer could use the endpoint to reproduce the behavior of the proprietary model without obtaining its stored files.

Which test would best evaluate this risk?

options.text: Embed hidden operating instructions in documents retrieved by the model
Insert mislabeled records into the storage location used for model training
Send systematic queries, and use the returned predictions to train a surrogate model
Send requests designed to consume the maximum available inference resources

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Send systematic queries, and use the returned predictions to train a surrogate model

Systematic querying followed by training a surrogate evaluates whether the endpoint reveals enough behavioral information to reproduce the proprietary model. Confidence scores can increase the usefulness of the responses when approximating decision boundaries.

Inserting mislabeled records tests training-data poisoning and requires access to the model’s training pipeline.

Sending resource-intensive requests tests susceptibility to model denial of service rather than extraction.

A tester has confirmed that a target service is affected by a specific vulnerability. An AI-assisted exploitation engine reviews the finding, matches it to a compatible exploit module, and prepares the exploit for use against the target.

Which part of the ethical-hacking process is being advanced by this activity?

options.text: Scanning the network for additional live hosts
Maintaining persistence after a successful compromise

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Gaining access through vulnerability exploitation

Matching a verified vulnerability to an exploit and preparing that exploit advances the gaining-access phase. The purpose is no longer to discover or characterize the weakness but to use it to obtain system access.

Network scanning identifies hosts, ports, and services before exploitation decisions are made.

Enumeration extracts service-specific information such as users, shares, or policies rather than attempting system compromise.

Persistence occurs after access has already been gained and focuses on retaining that access across later sessions or reboots.

questions.stem:
An attacker runs the following command on a compromised Linux system (without quotes):

" su root"

What stage in the MITRE ATT&CK Framework is the attacker most likely in?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Privilege escalation

" su root" is a Linux command that switches the current user to the root user. The root user is a highly privileged administrative account. 

Privilege escalation is a MITRE ATT&CK Framework stage where an attacker tries to increase their privileges and bypass security controls. Switching to root is a good example of a privilege escalation. 

The other answers are legitimate stages of the MITRE ATT&CK Framework but are not as directly related to the command " su root": 

Reconnaissance: Attackers look for targets and ways to access target systems
Resource development: Infrastructure, software, and information to support the management of compromised hosts is developed
Impact: Activities related to destroying data or preventing targets from accessing it

questions.stem: Which action should be taken to mitigate the impact of a potential Key Reinstallation Attack (KRACK) against WPA2?

options.text: Enforcing the use of HTTPS for all online transactions
Increasing the Wi-Fi network's RTS threshold
Applying patches and updates to Wi-Fi devices and infrastructure

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Applying patches and updates to Wi-Fi devices and infrastructure

The most effective countermeasure against the Key Reinstallation AttacK (KRACK) vulnerability is to apply all available patches and updates to Wi-Fi devices and infrastructure, as these updates are designed to address the specific issue. 

Switching to 802.11ac does not inherently solve the KRACK vulnerability. HTTPS is good practice for data in transit but is separate from Wi-Fi security. Adjusting the RTS threshold will not protect against KRACK.

It sends slow, incomplete HTTP headers to disrupt a web server’s operations
It rapidly floods a server with full HTTP requests

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: It sends slow, incomplete HTTP bodies to exhaust a web server’s resources

An R-U-Dead-Yet (RUDY) attack is a type of "low and slow" denial of service (DoS) attack that targets HTTP bodies by sending extremely slow and incomplete HTTP POST bodies. This approach keeps connections open for extended periods, consuming server resources until legitimate users are unable to access the service. RUDY is designed to overwhelm connection capacity rather than generate high traffic volume.

Incomplete HTTP headers are characteristic of Slowloris attacks, which is a different type of low and slow DoS attack that delays HTTP header (not HTTP body) completion.

Rapid flooding with full HTTP requests aligns with volumetric DoS attacks, which aim to overwhelm bandwidth or processing capacity rather than hold connections open slowly.

Exploiting authentication mechanisms involves targeting weaknesses in login or credential systems and does not relate to the timed, connection-holding strategy used in RUDY attacks.

questions.stem: Why is it crucial to regularly backup data as a malware countermeasure?

options.text: To allow multiple users to access data simultaneously
To restore information in case of data loss due to malware attacks like ransomware

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: To restore information in case of data loss due to malware attacks like ransomware

Regular backups are essential to ensure that, in the event of a malware attack (like ransomware that encrypts user data), the data can be restored from a backup without paying a ransom or facing significant data loss. 

Storage capacity, multi-user access, and software updating aren't direct reasons for regular backups as a malware countermeasure.

questions.stem: Which concept emphasizes ensuring that only authorized parties can access specific data or systems?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Confidentiality

Confidentiality involves taking measures to ensure data is not accessed or disclosed to unauthorized individuals, entities, or processes.

Availability ensures that data and services are accessible when needed. Non-repudiation ensures that a party cannot deny the authenticity of their signature on a document or the sending of a message. Integrity ensures data remains unaltered and trustworthy.

questions.stem: Why is footprinting on the dark web considered riskier compared to the surface web?

options.text: It's less dense in information, making footprinting easy
Search engines actively monitor and report dark web activities
It uses HTTP exclusively, making browsing insecure
It has a higher concentration of malicious actors and content

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: It has a higher concentration of malicious actors and content

The dark web is notorious for having a higher concentration of malicious actors, illegal activities, and potentially harmful content. While it is not illegal to access the dark web, many of the sites have illegal content. 

The dark web mainly uses .onion sites accessed via Tor, which employs encryption. Regular search engines don't index dark web content. The dark web contains vast amounts of information, though it may be harder to navigate and find relevant data.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of using encryption in information security?

options.text: To ensure data confidentiality and protect sensitive information
To provide real-time monitoring of network traffic
To prevent the loss of data during hardware failure

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: To ensure data confidentiality and protect sensitive information

Encryption is a technique used to convert plaintext data into a secure and unreadable format called ciphertext. It is primarily used to protect the confidentiality of sensitive information, ensuring that even if unauthorized individuals gain access to the data, they won't be able to decipher it. 

The other options describe different aspects of information security, but they wouldn't be achieved using encryption.

questions.stem: What is a primary security advantage of stateless protocols like those used in RESTful web services?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Reduced vulnerability to session-based attacks

A primary security advantage of stateless protocols, like those used in RESTful web services, is the reduced vulnerability to session-based attacks. Since stateless protocols do not require the server to retain user session information, it minimizes the risk of attacks that exploit session data, such as session hijacking or fixation. 

Stateless protocols are not inherently designed to enhance graphics, automate authentication, or increase processing speeds.

questions.stem: What is the role of a WAF in defending against SQL injection?

options.text: To analyze and filter incoming web traffic for SQL injection attempts
To automatically patch SQL injection vulnerabilities in web applications
To physically separate the web server from the database server
To accelerate web traffic and reduce the load on web servers

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: To analyze and filter incoming web traffic for SQL injection attempts

A Web Application Firewall ( WAF) defends against SQL injection by analyzing and filtering incoming web traffic to identify and block potential SQL injection attempts. It acts as a shield between the web application and the user, checking for malicious data that might exploit SQL injection vulnerabilities. 

A WAF does not provide physical separation, accelerate traffic, or patch application vulnerabilities directly.

questions.stem: What technique recycles session identifiers at critical stages to prevent token reuse?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Token rotation

Token rotation replaces the current session identifier with a newly generated value at security-sensitive stages, such as after successful authentication or a privilege change. Invalidating the previous identifier reduces the opportunity for an attacker to reuse a captured or previously known token.

Session timeout terminates a session after a defined period of inactivity or maximum duration, but it does not replace the identifier while the session remains active.

The Secure attribute instructs a browser to transmit a session cookie only over a Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure (HTTPS) connection. It protects the cookie during transmission but does not rotate its value.

Internet Protocol (IP) address binding associates a session with a particular source address, but it does not replace the session identifier and may cause problems when legitimate users’ addresses change.

questions.stem:
During an authorized investigation of a compromised workstation, an analyst finds a hidden file containing usernames, passwords, search terms, and fragments of chat messages in the exact order the user typed them. The entries include characters entered into applications that use encrypted network connections.

Which technique best explains the evidence?

options.text: Recording authentication tokens from browser storage
Extracting password hashes from system memory

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Capturing and recording user keystrokes

A keylogger records keyboard input as the user enters it, allowing it to collect credentials, messages, search terms, and other typed information. Because the capture occurs at the endpoint before the applications encrypt their network traffic, the log can contain readable input from encrypted sessions.

Extracting password hashes from system memory retrieves stored or cached authentication material. It would not normally produce an ordered record of everything the user typed across multiple applications.

Intercepting credentials from network traffic captures data transmitted over the network. Properly encrypted connections would prevent the attacker from reading the typed content directly from intercepted packets.

questions.stem: Which cloud computing characteristic allows the automatic scaling of resources based on service demand?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Rapid elasticity

Rapid elasticity is a cloud computing characteristic that allows services to be elastically provisioned and released to scale rapidly outward and inward according to the demand. This means that resources can be automatically scaled up or down based on service demand. 

Resource pooling refers to the provider’s ability to serve multiple consumers with provisioned resources. Broad network access allows services to be accessed through standard mechanisms by varied thin or thick client platforms. Measured service means cloud systems automatically control and optimize resource use by leveraging a metering capability.

questions.stem: Annabelle is gathering information about a target's website. She wants to see the hosting history of the website. Which tool can she use to achieve this?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Netcraft

Netcraft is a website that will give you hosting history for websites. It will provide the owner of the netblock that contains the IP address. Netcraft can also tell you what operating system the web server is running on. 

Wappalyzer is a browser plugin that can tell you about the technology stack of a website, but it will not provide information about the hosting history. Google Trends showcases search trends over time. Bleeping Computer is a website that offers news and resources about cybersecurity, not a tool for website footprinting.

While encryption, penetration testing, and access management are all essential security measures, they are not the primary functions of a honeypot.

questions.stem:
A web server accepts HTTP PUT requests for a writable directory without requiring authorization. A tester sends a PUT request containing a server-side script and can later access the uploaded file through its URL.

How is the vulnerability being exploited?

options.text: By identifying supported methods with an OPTIONS request
By uploading unauthorized files to the server
By deleting an existing resource with a DELETE request
By retrieving a protected resource with a GET request

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: By uploading unauthorized files to the server

The HTTP PUT method sends a representation to a specified resource location and may create or replace the resource. When a web server permits unauthenticated PUT requests to a writable directory, an attacker may upload an unauthorized file, including a script that the server could later execute.

A GET request retrieves a resource. It may be used to access the malicious file after upload, but it does not place the file on the server.

An OPTIONS request identifies the communication methods or features supported by a resource. It may help enumerate enabled HTTP methods but does not upload content.

A DELETE request removes a resource from the server rather than creating or replacing one.

questions.stem:
An attacker gets a non-technical target to click a link that displays a "YOUR COMPUTER HAS BEEN COMPROMISED" popup. The attacker tells the target that they can resolve the issue for them if the user provides their login credentials. 

This is an example of what social engineering technique?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Quid pro quo

Quid pro quo (Latin for "something for something") are social engineering techniques that involve an attacker getting the target to perform an act in exchange for something else. For example, maybe the target will be prompted to provide their password in exchange for IT work to remove a virus. 

Contact spamming occurs when an attacker gains access to a list of contacts and sends messages to those contacts to perform some type of attack or social engineering technique. 

Baiting is the act of leaving something physical somewhere (e.g., a USB stick in a parking lot) and waiting for a target to pick it up and use it. 

Tailgating is entering a restricted facility by coming in with or immediately behind authorized entrants.

questions.stem:
A web application asks an AI model to generate a database query from a user's natural-language request. The application sends the generated query directly to the database engine without validating or constraining it first. A manipulated request causes the model to generate an unintended destructive query that the database executes.

Which AI application vulnerability best describes the design flaw?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Insecure output handling

Insecure output handling occurs when generated model output is passed to another component without appropriate validation or controls. Here, the critical flaw is that the application treats generated SQL as trusted executable input to the database.

Prompt injection concerns manipulation of the model through instructions in its input. This may contribute to an attack path but does not describe the downstream design flaw being tested.

Model denial of service exhausts model resources or availability rather than causing a database to execute unvalidated generated output.

Training data poisoning alters data used to train or influence a model rather than exploiting unsafe handling of an inference-time response.

optionExplanations.A:

In a quid pro quo attack, the attacker offers something in return for information or action from the victim. This often leverages the victim's willingness to help or their desire for the quid (the thing of value being offered by the attacker). 

Impersonation involves pretending to be someone else, waterholing involves compromising websites the target frequently visits, and whaling is a targeted form of phishing aimed at high-profile targets.

questions.stem: What distinguishes an ethical hacker from a black hat hacker?

options.text: Black hat hackers are always more skilled than ethical hackers
Ethical hackers only hack into their own systems
Ethical hackers use different tools than black hat hackers
Ethical hackers have permission to break into the systems they test

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Ethical hackers have permission to break into the systems they test

The main difference between an ethical hacker and a black hat hacker is permission and intent. Ethical hackers have explicit permission to test systems, while black hat hackers do not.

Ethical hackers often use many of the same tools that black hat hackers do and are just as skilled. Ethical hackers do not only hack their own systems but also always have permission before hacking systems belonging to others.

questions.stem: Which application flaw pertains to the risk posed by third-party components, such as libraries or plugins, that an application relies on?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Insecure dependency usage

Insecure dependency usage or insecure third-party components are risks associated with vulnerabilities present in third-party libraries, frameworks, or plugins that an application might be dependent on. If these components have vulnerabilities and aren't updated, they can expose the entire application to risk. 

Insecure session management relates to user session issues. Misconfigured Content Security Policy (CSP) could lead to bypasses and unwanted script execution. Path traversal attacks are about navigating file directories.
